answer_summary: X is the neutral, closed-shell, aldehyde-functionalized fluorinated hexagonal polyamide excised from a COF-7 hexagonal pore. Its smallest repeat is one C2 half plus one D4-derived tetrafluoroterephthaloyl linker, C27H14F4N2O3; six repeats close the ring to give C162H84F24N12O18.
assumptions: Problem input: C2 is the pictured tetratopic tetraamine with one central stilbene olefin; D4 is the pictured 2,3,5,6-tetrafluoroterephthaldehyde.
Problem input: AcOH condensation gives the depicted Kagome imine COF-7, whose selected hexagonal boundary contains six C2 halves, six D4 linkers, and twelve condensation links.
Trusted general chemistry law: buffered NaClO2/NaH2PO4 oxidation converts Ar-N=CH-Ar imines to Ar-NH-C(=O)-Ar amides while preserving the scaffold.
Trusted general chemistry law: reductive ozonolysis with O3 then Me2S cleaves Ar-CH=CH-Ar to two Ar-CHO termini.
Structural convention: bonds in benzene rings are represented by the aromatic bond-order constructor rather than one arbitrary Kekule resonance form.
